{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (HDI Site Development, Hosting and Revenue Share Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.2 — verified findings and proposed positions

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement on behalf of the Company. Eighteen rules were assessed: seven clauses sit at or above our playbook position and require no redline; six clauses deviate on a material term; five expected protections are entirely absent from the document.

The most serious problems are omissions rather than bad drafting. The Agreement contains **no indemnification of any kind**, **no intellectual property ownership provision**, and **no limitation of liability or cap**. HDI builds and hosts the Site, supplies the software and technology, and holds our Content, user information and customer data, so the absence of an HDI IP-infringement indemnity, of any statement of who owns the Site, deliverables and customer data, and of any liability cap leaves us with unlimited exposure and no title to what we are funding. We have inserted preferred-position language for each (new Section 9(c) indemnity, new Section 5.5 ownership, new Section 10.9 mutual cap with uncapped Excluded Claims).

The key commercial deviation is the **exit economics**. Section 4.1 gives both parties a convenience right on 90 days' notice, but Section 4.2(a) charges the Company alone a Termination Payment of 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 — measured against gross Net Sales rather than fees, uncapped, and triggered by any Company termination other than the narrow Section 1.6 launch-failure carve-out. On illustrative numbers that is roughly $600,000 against roughly $140,000 of three months' fees, which renders our convenience right illusory. We have proposed deletion under the liquidated-damages rule and, in the alternative, a three-month fee cap with no payment where we terminate for HDI's failure or breach. The Section 6.1 exclusivity compounds this: it runs for the full auto-renewing term with no performance-based release, so the only exit from the restriction is a termination that may trigger the Section 4.2 payment.

Several counterparty-favourable terms are noted but expressly **not** flagged: Section 6.3's heavier two-year post-term restriction on HDI, the Section 3.4 inspection cost allocation (HDI bears its own fees), the absence of any change-of-control termination trigger, and the pure revenue-share fee structure with no minimum commitment.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / proposal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | No indemnity, hold-harmless or defence language anywhere; fails even the fallback. Insert HDI indemnity (third-party IP, breach of law, HDI-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) as new Section 9(c) with notice/control/cooperation mechanics. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | No ownership or assignment clause. Add Section 5.5: Company owns the Site, deliverables and customer data with HDI assignment; HDI retains background IP and grants a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | No cap and no consequential-damages exclusion; both parties face unlimited liability. Insert Section 10.9: mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, mutual consequential exclusion, uncapped Excluded Claims. Fallback: plain 12 months' fees. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | Section 6.1 restriction runs for the full auto-renewing term with no performance-based release. Cap our restriction at 12 months from the Effective Date and release it automatically on HDI's failure to meet the Site operational date or any service level, delivery date or performance obligation. HDI's brand right and Section 6.3 left intact. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | Section 4.2 Termination Payment is measured on gross Net Sales, uncapped, and triggered by any Company termination. Delete Section 4.2 and conform the Section 4 heading; three-month fee cap acceptable as fallback. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | Notice period and HDI-side exit sit at the fallback and are not flagged; the Section 4.2(a) payment makes our exit illusory. Cap the Termination Payment at three months' fees and confirm no payment where we terminate for HDI's launch failure or breach. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | Section 6.1 sits at the fallback: defined product set plus named competitors, term-only with no post-term tail, exitable within 12 months, with closeout/Joan Cook and Globix carve-outs. Elastic "companies similar to" wording and the absence of an acquisitions/internal-development carve-out are noted, not redlined. |
| Medium | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | Section 10.3 is silent on consent, leaving HDI free to assign (including to a competitor) together with our confidential data obligations. Add a Company affiliate/successor carve-out plus a reasonable-consent gate and no-competitor limit on HDI. No change-of-control trigger exists, which favours us. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | Section 3.4 notice, business-hours conduct and cost allocation meet or exceed our position, but there is no frequency limit at all. Cap the inspection right at once per twelve months. Inspection by HDI's General Manager noted only, given Section 8.2 confidentiality. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | Section 10.5 selects New York law (our preferred position) and disapplies conflicts principles; no foreign venue and no arbitration. Absence of an express exclusive-venue clause naming New York County courts is noted, not redlined. |
| Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | Section 1.4 grants access to "the Company" only, and Section 10.3's "no other person shall acquire or have any rights" affirmatively excludes our Affiliates and contractors with no path to add them. Extend the grant to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf and carve them, plus an express successor transfer right, out of Section 10.3. Written-notice mechanic offered as fallback. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | No MFN, no-less-favourable, best-terms or matching obligation anywhere; Section 3 is a fixed revenue share. Preferred position; no redline. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | Section 3.1 is a pure revenue share (30% of Net Sales above an $11,000 monthly floor) with no take-or-pay, shortfall or volume cap, plus a standing 90-day exit under Section 4.1. Preferred position; the Section 4.2 exit fee and Section 6.1 exclusivity are addressed under their own rules. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | No non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant anywhere, including around the Section 5.4 liaison appointments. Preferred position; no redline. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | Successive one-year renewals are acceptable, but the 90-day non-renewal window exceeds the 60-day fallback ceiling. Shorten to 30 days (60 days as fallback). No reminder or uplift cap needed given the revenue-share fee structure. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and | No exit, migration, data return/export or deletion language anywhere, in a hosting arrangement where HDI holds our Content and customer data. Insert Section 4.3: up to six months' transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, 30-day return in machine-readable format, deletion with written certification. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | Section 9 contains only corporate reps and the Globix acknowledgement; no workmanlike, conformance, compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty and no remedy. Add Section 9(c) at the preferred position with repair/replace/re-perform/refund at HDI's option; shorter conformance period available as fallback. Absence of an "AS IS" disclaimer mitigates. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a | No insurance obligation at all, although HDI hosts the Site and accesses our Content and data under Section 8.1. Insert Section 10.9 at preferred limits (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request). Fallback: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following are identified in the findings as walk-away territory or as triggering a walk-away condition. We should not sign without movement on each.

1. **No HDI IP-infringement indemnity (INDEMN, § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a).** HDI builds and hosts the Site and supplies the software and technology; the total absence of any indemnity is walk-away territory and fails even the fallback.
2. **Affiliates and contractors affirmatively excluded from the licence (LICENSE, § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and).** Section 10.3's "no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement" excludes our Affiliates and contractors from the granted rights with no mechanism to add them — the rule's walk-away trigger.
3. **Unlimited HDI inspection rights (AUDIT, § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and).** Section 3.4 has no frequency limit; unlimited audits fall below the fallback and into walk-away territory. The once-per-twelve-month cap is the minimal fix.
4. **No vendor insurance (INSURANCE, § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a).** A vendor processing our Customer Data with no coverage obligation at all is walk-away territory under the rule.
5. **Full-term exclusivity with no performance exit (EXCLUSIVITY, § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a).** Section 6.1 fails the fallback and approaches walk-away territory: exclusive dealing for the full auto-renewing term, where the only escape is a termination that may itself trigger the Section 4.2 Termination Payment. We propose the fallback rather than deletion because Section 6.3 gives us a matching, longer restriction on HDI.

**Closely related priority, though not designated walk-away:** the missing liability cap (LOL-CAP) leaves both sides with unlimited exposure and fails both preferred and fallback positions; and the Section 4.2 Termination Payment (LD / T4C) is uncapped and measured on gross Net Sales.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Circulate the marked-up draft** containing the five insertions (Section 9(c) indemnity, Section 9(c) performance warranty, Section 5.5 ownership, Section 10.9 mutual liability cap, Section 10.9 insurance, Section 4.3 transition assistance) and the six deviation redlines, each with a `[Playbook]` comment explaining the change and the available fallback.
2. **Confirm the LICENSE redline in the executed draft.** That item's verification is recorded as *repaired* rather than clean; we will re-check that the Section 1.4 extension and the Section 10.3 carve-out read together correctly before the draft goes out.
3. **Escalate the exit economics to the business team.** We need the illustrative modelling behind the Section 4.2 formula (the roughly $600,000 versus roughly $140,000 comparison at $2M annual Net Sales) to support either deletion or the three-month fee cap, and confirmation of whether HDI's build and programming cost recovery justifies any exit fee at all.
4. **Prepare a two-tier negotiation brief:** (a) the five walk-away items above, on which we hold; (b) the fallback landing zones we can concede — 12 months' fees without the USD 1,000,000 floor on the cap, a three-month fee cap in place of deleting Section 4.2, a 60-day non-renewal window, E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M insurance, a shorter warranty conformance period, and a written-notice mechanic for adding Affiliates.
5. **Flag the reciprocity question on indemnity.** We did not add a Company indemnity; if HDI asks, a narrow indemnity limited to Company-supplied Content is acceptable.
6. **Hold the noted-but-unflagged points in reserve** for use only if the Agreement is reopened for other reasons: an acquisitions/internal-development carve-out and an agreed competitor list in Section 6.1, and an express exclusive-venue provision naming the state and federal courts in New York County under Section 10.5."}
